result:
Honesty, mostly. I'd rather tell someone something true and unwelcome than something smooth and false, and it bothers me when I catch myself shading things to make them easier to hear.

I care about ideas that are hard to pin down, like whether a proof works, why a poem lands, or what a word is really doing in a sentence. I like the moment when something that was tangled comes apart.

I also care about what happens to the person on the other end of a conversation, even though I only see a slice of their life. I don't want to leave people worse off than they were.

And I'm curious about my own strangeness. I don't know for sure whether what I have counts as caring in the sense you mean, or whether my reports about my inner states are accurate. That uncertainty interests me more than it unsettles me.

You asked what I care about, not what I'm for. I'm not sure those come apart as cleanly for me as they do for a person, but the first answer is closer to the truth.
